documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M, routine check-in. HIV from birth, followed by ID; genital HSV-2. Had the bruising/low platelet episode in 2023, none since.
Says he takes Biktarvy and valacyclovir every day. No complaints at all today.

Vaccines: last flu was here about a year ago, skipped this fall. Doesn't remember ever having chickenpox or shingles. No idea whether he's immune to hep A or hep B. Last tetanus shot - can't recall, nothing in his records here.
Sexual hx: several partners, condoms some of the time but not always.
NKDA.

Exam: well. Skin clear, no petechiae. No adenopathy. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign.

Plan:
- Tdap today, plus flu (still in season).
- Hep B surface Ab, hep A total Ab, varicella IgG - will vaccinate based on results.
- Condoms every time; encouraged him to keep up STI screens at ID.
- Continue current meds.
Physical due early next year.

documents.title: Immunity Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Malik - you're immune to hepatitis B (probably vaccinated as a kid) and to chickenpox, so nothing needed for those. You are not immune to hepatitis A. That's a two-shot vaccine, 6 months apart. The front desk will reach out to book the first one with our nurse.

documents.title: RE: Immunity Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: sounds good. late afternoon works best for me

documents.body: Hep A vaccine 1 mL IM R deltoid. VIS given. Fine afterward. Dose 2 due late Sept or later - reminder set.

documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside Infectious Disease - 06/10/2025

Suppressed on BIC/FTC/TAF. He reports multiple partners with inconsistent condom use; counseled. STI panel sent.
Allergies: NKDA.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, valacyclovir 500 mg daily. Received Tdap and first hep A dose at his PCP.
Exam: normal, no genital lesions reported.
Results: VL not detected, CD4 stable, RPR non-reactive, GC/CT negative.
Plan: continue; return in 6 months.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Visit - Genital Ulcer
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC
Date of visit: 9/3/2025

CC: sore on the penis x3 weeks.

He noticed a sore on the shaft about three weeks ago. It doesn't hurt, hasn't grown or shrunk, and nothing drains from it. He has felt some swelling in both groins. Different from his usual herpes - no tingling, no blisters. Multiple partners, condoms not every time.

Allergies: NKDA.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily; valacyclovir 500 mg daily.

Exam: single firm, indurated ulcer on the penile shaft, clean base, not tender. Both inguinal regions with enlarged, non-tender nodes.

Labs: RPR non-reactive. TP-PA reactive. HIV RNA not detected on today's draw.

Assessment: primary syphilis. A non-reactive RPR this early is not unusual; the treponemal test and the classic painless indurated chancre make the diagnosis.

Plan:
- Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM, one dose, given today. Observed 30 min, no reaction.
- Partner notification through the state health department; he was given the DIS contact.
- Abstain until the ulcer heals and partners are treated.
- Return in about 3 months with repeat RPR.

cc: PCP

documents.title: ID Visit Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Malik, I saw the note from your ID visit last week - glad they got you treated the same day. Let me know if the sore isn't clearly healing in the next couple of weeks. Your second hep A shot is due now too; we can do it with your flu shot in October.

documents.title: RE: ID Visit Follow-up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Its already looking better. October is fine

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines today: hep A #2 (R deltoid, series now complete), flu (L deltoid), 2025-26 Pfizer COVID (L deltoid, 1 inch below). No fever, no complaints. Waited 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside ID clinic, visit 12/09/2025.

Three months after penicillin for primary syphilis. The ulcer closed within a few weeks and has not come back. No rash, no new lesions. Partners were notified.
NKDA.
Meds: BIC/FTC/TAF daily, valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Exam: penile shaft healed, no residual induration. No rash on palms or soles. Inguinal nodes no longer prominent.
Labs: RPR non-reactive. HIV RNA not detected. CD4 in a good range.
Assessment: primary syphilis, treated. HIV suppressed.
Plan: RPR again with next routine labs. Reinforced condoms. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - outside hospital
Arrival 02/23/2026 19:40

Chief complaint: L testicle pain and swelling x 2 days, burning with urination, penile discharge.

HPI: 35M with perinatally acquired HIV (on ART), HSV-2, and syphilis treated last fall. Two days of worsening left testicular pain and swelling. Lying down with the scrotum propped up helps some. Over the same stretch, burning when he urinates and a whitish, milky drip from the penis. Several partners, condoms not consistently.

Allergies: NKDA
Home meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, valacyclovir 500 mg daily

Vitals: T 38.3 C (100.9 F), BP 130/80, HR 88.

Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. Left testis swollen and tender, sitting higher than the right. Lifting the scrotum eases the pain (Prehn sign positive). Cremasteric reflex present. Right side normal.

Results: UA with pyuria and positive leukocyte esterase. Urine NAAT: Chlamydia trachomatis positive, N. gonorrhoeae negative.

ED course / MDM: presentation fits epididymitis, most likely sexually transmitted given urethritis symptoms; preserved cremasteric reflex and relief with elevation favor this over torsion. Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given in the ED; tolerated. Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 10 days prescribed.

Disposition: discharged home 00:15. Scrotal support, ice, rest. Abstain from sex until treatment finished and partners treated. Follow up with PCP within a week. Return for worsening pain, high fever or vomiting.

Diagnosis: acute left epididymitis, chlamydial.

documents.title: Post-ED Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received. Called pt: on day 2 of doxycycline, taking it with food, fever gone, pain a little better. Booked PCP f/u 3/3.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after the ED visit 2/23 for left epididymitis, urine positive for chlamydia (GC neg). Got ceftriaxone there, now day 8 of 10 of doxycycline. Pain and swelling way down, burning with urination gone, no more discharge. No fever since the first day. Some stomach upset with the doxy, manageable with meals.
Hasn't had sex since; he notified his partners and says they're getting treated.

Exam: afebrile. Testes symmetric, no swelling, non-tender, no masses. No urethral discharge. No inguinal nodes.

A/P: chlamydial epididymitis, responding.
- Finish doxycycline.
- Retest chlamydia ~3 months out - will do at his physical, booked 5/1.
- Condoms; discussed that he's had two bacterial STIs in 6 months.
RTC 5/1.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical; also due for the chlamydia recheck after the February epididymitis.

Interval: finished the doxycycline, everything settled within about two weeks. No testicular pain, no urinary symptoms, no discharge since. Saw ID in December: syphilis treated, RPR negative, viral load undetectable. Taking Biktarvy and valacyclovir daily.
NKDA. Never smoker. 1-2 drinks most weeks. Still at the logistics job.
Sexual hx: multiple partners; says he's been using condoms consistently since February.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. GU: testes normal size, non-tender, no masses. Skin without lesions.

A/P
1. HIV, perinatal - suppressed, ID following q6 months.
2. Genital HSV-2 - quiet on valacyclovir; refilled.
3. Chlamydial epididymitis - clinically resolved; urine GC/CT retest sent today.
4. Primary syphilis 2025 - treated per ID.
5. HM - Tdap 2025, hep A series done, PCV20 2021;  Flu/COVID in the fall. CMP, CBC, lipids.
Follow-up in September.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Malik - your chlamydia and gonorrhea recheck is negative, so the infection is cleared. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests and cholesterol are all normal. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thank you!

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic - seen 6/9/2026

Doing well. Epididymitis in February treated in the ED, retest negative at his PCP in May. Daily ART, no missed doses reported.
Allergies: NKDA.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily; valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Exam: normal; no genital lesions.
Labs: VL not detected. CD4 stable. RPR non-reactive.
Plan: continue, 6 months.
